newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori hits new popularity low - poll.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori hits new popularity low - poll.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori ended a turbulent week of street protests and ministerial resignations with the backing of less than one in five Peruvians, a poll published on Saturday revealed.
According to the survey by local pollsters Imasen, just 19 percent of 400 people questioned in Lima last week approved of Fujimori's government, compared to 39.5 percent in late May.
It was the lowest popularity level for the 58-year-old leader in seven years of power.

After riding a crest of public approval at the end of Lima's four-month hostage crisis, Fujimori's popularity has plummeted with a series of scandals over abuses by intelligence services and interference with press freedom.

Public outrage intensified last week when the government revoked the nationality of Israeli-born businessman Baruch Ivcher whose television network had broken a series of stories including torture and phone tapping by intelligence agents.
The bugging revelations and Ivcher's case provoked the resignation of three ministers and massive street protests.
The Imasen poll showed that 94.3 percent of Peruvians felt the goverment should thoroughly investigate the accusations made on Ivcher's Frecuencia Latina network and punish those found guilty.
No margin of error was given for the poll.
